practice_description.medium: On-chain generative art, software, blockchain-native digital art
practice_description.practice_summary: Art Blocks is a platform for on-chain generative art where artists upload JavaScript scripts to Ethereum smart contracts, producing unique outputs at mint time. It pioneered the curated generative NFT model and is expanding via Art Blocks Engine into institutional partnerships.
practice_description.methodology: Artists write generative scripts in JavaScript that are stored immutably on the Ethereum blockchain. At mint time, a pseudo-random hash seed determines the unique output. The platform operates through multiple tiers: Curated (highest curation, ending at project 500), Explorations, and Engine (white-label for institutional partners). 90% of collections are now fully on-chain including all dependencies. The curation board reviews submissions for the Curated collection based on technical innovation and aesthetic quality.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Art Blocks demonstrates how generative art can function as primary material in a curated system, with each output determined by on-chain parameters. Its Engine model shows how generative infrastructure can be extended to institutional contexts, directly relevant to A(DAI)'s graph-curated exhibition concept.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes. Each Art Blocks output is a generative artwork determined by algorithmic parameters. These outputs could serve as substrate layers in a compositional system, as the scripts themselves are modular, deterministic, and replayable from on-chain data.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Limited. Individual projects are self-contained rather than relational. However, the broader Art Blocks collection creates an implicit network of stylistic and technical relationships between projects and artists that could be made explicit through graph-based curation.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: No. Once minted, Art Blocks outputs are fixed by their hash seed. The generative moment occurs once at mint time. However, newer features like PostParams suggest movement toward post-mint parameter modification.

works.title: Chromie Squiggle
works.description: Erick Calderon's founding project -- simple colored curves generated from on-chain hash seeds. Became the iconic identity of Art Blocks.
works.relevance: Demonstrates the core Art Blocks mechanic of script-to-hash generative output and on-chain preservation.

works.title: Fidenza
works.description: Tyler Hobbs' flow-field generative art project that became one of the most celebrated generative NFT collections.
works.relevance: Showed how generative algorithms produce aesthetically sophisticated outputs that function as standalone artworks, relevant to art-as-substrate thinking.

works.title: Art Blocks 500 (Complete Collection)
works.description: The finite set of 500 flagship projects across Curated, Playground, Factory, Presents, Collaborations, and Explorations categories, completed November 2025.
works.relevance: Represents a deliberate framing of a platform's output as a complete, bounded collection -- a curatorial act that transforms infrastructure into a defined body of work.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Art Blocks treats blockchain infrastructure as a creative medium. The smart contract architecture -- where scripts live on-chain and outputs are generated at mint time -- is itself a form of protocol design that shapes artistic possibility. The curation board model, Engine partnerships, and minting mechanisms (Dutch auctions, allowlists) are governance-as-design decisions.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Art Blocks Engine: a white-label smart contract infrastructure that allows institutions (Pace Gallery, Bright Moments) to deploy their own branded generative art platforms using Art Blocks' proven on-chain architecture. Also: the Minter Suite, an expandable set of minting mechanisms artists can select per-project.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Smart contracts are open-sourced on GitHub. On-chain art is immutably accessible -- anyone with a browser and Ethereum access can reconstruct any artwork. However, the platform itself is a venture-funded company ($6M raised), and the curation and Engine partnership models are proprietary. Individual artwork IP rights vary by artist.

governance_model.governance_detail: Governed by co-CEOs Erick Calderon and Jeff Davis. The Curated collection was managed by a curation board that reviewed submissions, though this program ended with project 500. Engine partnerships are negotiated institutionally. No DAO or token-based governance. Approximately 29 employees as of 2026.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Artists voluntarily submit projects and agree to platform terms. Collectors consent through the minting process. The on-chain nature means provenance is transparent and immutable.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo artist authorship is primary. The artist writes the generative script; the collector's mint triggers a unique output via hash seed. Collaborations series introduced co-authorship with institutional partners (Pace Gallery, Bright Moments).

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: The generative moment occurs once at mint time, when a pseudo-random hash seed determines the output. After minting, the artwork is static and permanently stored on-chain. The script can be re-executed at any time to reproduce the same output from the same seed. PostParams feature may allow post-mint parameter changes in future projects.

data_materiality.data_sources: On-chain hash seeds (pseudo-random numbers generated by the Randomizer contract), artist-written JavaScript scripts, and optional external assets (images, audio, video) stored on IPFS, Arweave, or Ethereum for Engine Flex projects.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Self-generated. Hash seeds are generated on-chain at mint time. Scripts are authored by artists and stored immutably on Ethereum. External assets for Flex projects are stored on decentralized infrastructure with verifiable provenance.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Art Blocks does not directly engage with embedding or latent spaces. The generative process is algorithmic (script-based) rather than model-based. However, the parameter space defined by each script's hash seed creates an implicit high-dimensional output space that maps seeds to visual outputs.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: No. Primarily visual outputs, though Engine Flex allows audio and video assets.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Primarily web-based -- artworks are rendered in-browser from on-chain scripts. Engine partnerships with Bright Moments have brought outputs into physical gallery contexts with live-minting events. The platform also supports high-resolution rendering for print output.

interoperability.composability: Moderate. Smart contracts are open-source and follow ERC-721 standards. The Graph subgraph indexes on-chain data publicly. Art Blocks Engine is explicitly designed as composable infrastructure for third parties. However, individual artworks are self-contained scripts rather than modular components.
interoperability.technical_openness: Open source smart contracts on GitHub. On-chain art is permanently accessible. Engine provides documented onboarding for institutional partners.

technical_approach.stack: Ethereum blockchain (ERC-721), Solidity smart contracts (Core V3, Admin ACL, Randomizer, Minter Suite), JavaScript (artist scripts), The Graph (indexing), IPFS and Arweave (external asset storage for Flex), web browser rendering. Supports multiple Ethereum networks including mainnet and Layer 2s.

network_position.scene_affiliation: Central hub of the on-chain generative art movement. Connected to the broader crypto-art ecosystem, institutional art world (Pace Gallery), generative art community, and creative coding communities. Bridges crypto-native and traditional art worlds through Engine partnerships.
network_position.connections: fx(hash) (fellow generative art platform, different chain), Rhizome (digital art preservation context), Bright Moments (Engine partner for live-minting events)

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Art Blocks' on-chain generative art archive and Engine infrastructure could serve as a data source for A(DAI)'s intelligence graph -- mapping relationships between generative artists, stylistic tendencies, and institutional partnerships. The open-source smart contracts and Graph subgraph provide accessible data for relational mapping. Art Blocks artists represent a key practitioner cohort for the digital arts field.
